g.text: A job-posting URL in. A truthful, one-page tailored resume out.
Core bet: deterministic Python does ~80% of the work at 0 tokens; the model is invoked only to author.
1 · CONTROL PLANE localhost only, no auth surface, no cloud dependency
Whole-file PUT was deliberately removed: a stale browser tab used to erase rows the agent had written. Row-scoped writes only.
2 · ORCHESTRATION PLANE agent/run.py - pure Python, flock-guarded, zero tokens
Stages 1-3 run in a thread pool (<= 8). All HTTP is urllib inside Python, never a model tool - so a new ATS host never raises a permission prompt.
HARD_DROP visa sponsorship refused · security clearance · ITAR / U.S.-person · citizenship required · posting removed -> dropped, 0 tokens spent
NEEDS_REVIEW entry-level title with no comp · comp ceiling < $100K · required language the candidate lacks · PERM filing markers (#LI-DNI)
False-positive guards: EEO boilerplate near 'citizenship' is ignored; an unresolved Greenhouse board token returns 'unresolved', never 'removed'.
Comp parser handles $182,800-$247,300 · $116,000 - $174,000 USD · $215-230K · flat ranges, and ignores '5-8 years'.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Why regex and not an LLM screen: free, deterministic, unit-testable, and auditable - a drop can always be explained by the sentence that caused it.
3 · AUTHORING PLANE the only place tokens are spent
inside ONE forked session - the vendored /resume-tailoring skill drives quality, not this repo's Python
The child NEVER writes job_queue.json or LIBRARY.md - it emits one staging JSON. All shared-file writes happen in the parent thread, so they cannot interleave.
--strict-mcp-config keeps 6 unused MCP servers out of context · 900s watchdog per role · a lost base session is detected, re-primed, and retried once.
4 · STATE PLANE plain files, git-diffable, no database, no migrations

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: queued -> needs_review -> resume_ready -> applied -> screen -> interviewing -> offer / rejected / dropped
The agent may only ever set dropped / needs_review / resume_ready. Everything from 'applied' onward is human-owned, and a regression guard refuses backward moves.
DESIGN PRIORITIES - what this system optimizes for, in order
· Skill loaded once, reused per job
· Telemetry splits fresh vs cache tokens
· Serial beats parallel here: one warm
· flock on agent/.lock - one run at a time
· Children write no shared state at all
· Atomic temp-file + rename on every save
· Auto-refresh never clobbers a live edit
· Status regression guard on every write
on the next run - no lost work
· The agent never marks a role 'applied'
· Every drop carries the exact reason
· Coverage + gap report beside each resume
· One-click Build / Drop on parked rows
· needs_review is a feature, not a failure:
it is where the system admits it should
TRADE-OFFS TAKEN, AND WHAT COMES NEXT
· JSON files over a database - the queue stays git-diffable, greppable, and readable inside a Claude session; ops cost is zero.
· Regex screening over an LLM screen - eligibility rules are cheap, deterministic, and every drop is explainable by the sentence that triggered it.
· The tailoring logic lives in a vendored third-party skill, not in this repo's Python - quality can be edited as prose without touching code.
· Orchestrator owns mechanics, model owns judgment - the boundary is drawn where determinism stops being possible, not where it is convenient.
· stdlib-only Python and a single-file UI - clone and run; nothing to install but Chrome and one npm package.
Next: cron/systemd + Task Scheduler parity · a recorded-fixture test harness for ATS adapters · an eval set that scores coverage claims against
real callbacks · multi-candidate libraries so the system serves more than one person.
